betterCitation: Antonio Machado, Proverbios y cantares XXIX, lines 1 to 4, Campos de Castilla (1912) (trans. Betty Jean Craige, 1979)
reason:
Refuted. I attacked the hedge as instructed and it got worse, not better, on three separate counts, and the hedge is the kind that rides the carry into a month and ships.
1. THE ENGLISH WORDING IS ATTRIBUTED, NOT LOCATED, AND THE ONE REFERENCE THAT NAMES THE BOOK CONTRADICTS IT. Every place I could reach that carries 'Wanderer, your footsteps are / the road, and nothing more' is a quote aggregator, a blog or a devotional post (goodreads, quotepark, whatshouldireadnext, hermitary.com/thatch/?p=447, thealchemyofpilgrimage.wordpress.com). Not one gives a page. Wikiquote, the only source that cites the volume with any care, credits Betty Jean Craige with a materially different rendering: 'Wanderer, your footprints are / the path, and nothing else; / wanderer, there is no path, / the path is made by walking.' Footprints not footsteps, path not road, nothing else not nothing more. Both cannot be Craige's printed text. So the source line's claim 'English wording attributed to Betty Jean Craige' puts a specific translator's name on specific words that the only book-citing reference says are not hers. That is exactly the confident false citation the standard forbids, and the hedge in the note does not cure it, because the byline still reads as a credit.
2. THE WORK AND DATE IN THE SOURCE LINE ARE WRONG. The source says 'Poesías completas (1917)'. Proverbios y cantares XXIX first appeared in Campos de Castilla (1912): the Liter-Alia scholarly page at scalar.usc.edu states 'Poema extraído de Campos de Castilla, XXIX Proverbios y cantares, 1912', and Wikiquote gives the same first collection. The card would print a five-year error in the one field a reader can check.
3. NOTHING ELSE IN THE CITATION IS FIXED EITHER. The translation year is given as 1978 in the Internet Archive catalogue record for selectedpoemsofa0000mach and as 1979 in the press and in secondary citations, and I could not settle it. Page 143 is unconfirmed and stayed unconfirmed. The Internet Archive copy is lending restricted; its search-inside endpoint (ia-fts.archive.org) does not resolve from here, HathiTrust returned 403, and Google Books search returned no snippet. I could not open a single page of any printed edition. Under rule 30 a translated line carries a locatable citation naming the translator and the year of the published translation whose wording it uses, and this line satisfies none of those three.
I also tried to rescue it with a different published translation and could not, honestly. Robert Bly's Times Alone (Wesleyan, 1983) is reported not to contain this poem at all. The Poetry Foundation text '[Traveler, your footprints]' is credited to Mary G. Berg and Dennis Maloney, There Is No Road (White Pine Press, 2003), which is a 2003 wording and a different one. Alan Trueblood (Harvard, 1982) renders it differently again. The Spanish is settled and is the only settled thing here: 'Caminante, son tus huellas / el camino, y nada más; / caminante, no hay camino, / se hace camino al andar.'
betterCitation above fixes the work and the date only. It does NOT certify the English. Do not ship on it. This line should either be held until somebody opens Craige's printed page and reads the four lines off it, or be replaced by a rendering whose page can actually be seen.
